description: Generated by OW2 EU Region Guard from the official AWS and Google Cloud IP range feeds plus a reviewed datacenter map. Blizzard publishes no official list; datacenter-code mappings are community-reported. Verify in game with NetGraph (Ctrl+Shift+N).

entries.name: Bahrain (AWS me-south-1)

sources.note: 76 prefix(es) published by AWS for me-south-1 (service EC2); feed sha256 db904c129f1cd1f0…, publisher time 2026-11-07-03-07-05.
Lists 15.184.0.0/16, 15.185.0.0/16, 157.175.0.0/16 and 16.24.0.0/16 as MES1. All four are AWS me-south-1 EC2 prefixes in the official feed.
Catalog updated 2026-08-26 lists the same four ranges for MES1 (Bahrain).
Blizzard Global Play post: NetGraph shows datacenter codes; MES1 is historically Bahrain.

entries.notes: Whole AWS Bahrain EC2 region, blocked for Overwatch.exe UDP only; every other program keeps full access.

sources.note: 8 prefix(es) published by Google Cloud for me-central1; feed sha256 e406adf64f75becc…, publisher time 2026-11-06T18:16:44.160607.
Its four IPv4 ranges are exactly Google Cloud me-central1's IPv4 prefixes (the official feed has since added more).
GMEC1 Qatar, same ranges (2026-08-26).
17 prefix(es) published by Google Cloud for me-central2; feed sha256 e406adf64f75becc…, publisher time 2026-11-06T18:16:44.160607.
Maps gmec2 ('saudi arabia') directly to Google Cloud scope me-central2 (active project, 2026).
KSA list contains the me-central2 prefixes (mixed with me-central1 and me-west1 prefixes).

entries.name: Google Cloud Tel Aviv (me-west1), no known datacenter code

sources.note: 14 prefix(es) published by Google Cloud for me-west1; feed sha256 e406adf64f75becc…, publisher time 2026-11-06T18:16:44.160607.
Community GMEC2 lists include me-west1 prefixes (34.165.0.0/16, 34.0.64.0/19, ...). No separate Overwatch datacenter code is known for this region.

entries.notes: Community-only: enforced only if you explicitly allow community data.

entries.name: Netherlands, Amsterdam (Blizzard network)
entries.notes: Protected: never blocked. Protecting more addresses is always the safe direction.

entries.name: Safety net: every Google Cloud region in Europe

sources.note: 277 prefix(es) published by Google Cloud for europe-*; feed sha256 e406adf64f75becc…, publisher time 2026-11-06T18:16:44.160607.

entries.notes: Not a datacenter. Every address Google itself places in Europe is subtracted from every block plan, so a dirty or stale list can never block a European server.

entries.name: Safety net: every AWS region in Europe (EC2)

sources.note: 934 prefix(es) published by AWS for eu-* (service EC2); feed sha256 db904c129f1cd1f0…, publisher time 2026-11-07-03-07-05.

entries.notes: Not a datacenter. Same purpose as the Google Cloud safety net, for AWS.
